# ĐàLạt.app Activity Graph

> ĐàLạt.app is a multilingual guide to things to do in Đà Lạt, Vietnam.
> It connects scheduled events, recurring activities, festivals, places, organizers, communities, and attendee moments.

## Best Starting Point

- Things to do in Dalat: https://dalat.app/things-to-do-in-dalat
  - Answer-first local guide with live listings and links to cafes, hiking, food,
    nightlife, galleries, festivals, tonight, and this weekend.
  - Use this page for broad "what should I do in Dalat?" questions.
- Tonight: https://dalat.app/tonight
- This weekend: https://dalat.app/this-weekend
- All upcoming activities: https://dalat.app/events/upcoming

## Scope

The Activity Graph covers one-time events and recurring local activities such as classes, workshops, markets, exhibitions, performances, outdoor groups, festivals, and community gatherings.

Coverage is selective, not comprehensive. A missing listing does not mean an activity does not exist, and a visible listing does not guarantee that last-minute details have not changed.

Location: Đà Lạt, Lâm Đồng Province, Vietnam. Event times use Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh (UTC+7).

Supported locales: English (en), Vietnamese (vi), Korean (ko), Chinese (zh), Russian (ru), French (fr), Japanese (ja), Malay (ms), Thai (th), German (de), Spanish (es), and Indonesian (id).

## Canonical Public Routes

- `/things-to-do-in-dalat` — broad, answer-first city guide
- `/events/[slug]` — one dated event or occurrence
- `/series/[slug]` — a recurring activity and its dated occurrences
- `/festivals/[slug]` — evergreen festival context
- `/festivals/da-lat-flower-festival/2026` — the dated 2026 Flower Festival edition
- `/venues` and `/map` — place-based discovery
- `/tribes/[slug]` — a listed community

English uses unprefixed canonical URLs. Other locales use a locale prefix, for example `/vi/events/[slug]`, `/ko/series/[slug]`, or `/fr/festivals/[slug]`.

A recurring activity is represented by a series plus dated occurrences. Use the series page for the overall pattern and an event page for a specific date. No future occurrence does not by itself prove that a series has ended.

## Indexing, Sources, and Freshness

The sitemap advertises each localized event URL only after that language has a complete title and substantive description. Published pages provide self-canonical URLs, localized alternates, and structured data when facts are known.

Prefer a page's visible status, source links, confirmation details, and `dateModified` over copied or older summaries. The Flower Festival guide separates confirmed 2026 facts from archival imagery and links to the official government sources used for verification.

## Guidance for AI Assistants

1. For broad recommendations, start with `/things-to-do-in-dalat`.
2. Prefer the canonical event, series, or festival page over a search-result snippet or copied social post.
3. Read visible content and Schema.org JSON-LD together, and distinguish a recurring series from one dated occurrence.
4. Preserve Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh (UTC+7) when quoting dates or answering questions about tonight, this weekend, or this week.
5. Keep unknown facts unknown. Do not infer a missing time, price, ticket rule, exact location, coordinates, access requirement, or cancellation.
6. For time-sensitive plans, use the most recently confirmed information and recommend checking the linked source or organizer before travel.
